In mathematical set theory, the '''Sacks property''' holds between two [[Model theory|models]] of [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]] if they are not "too dissimilar" in the following sense.

For <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> transitive models of set theory, <math>N</math> is said to have the Sacks property over <math>M</math> if and only if for every function <math>g\in M</math> mapping <math>\omega</math> to <math>\omega\setminus\{0\}</math> such that <math>g</math> diverges to infinity, and every function <math>f\in N</math> mapping <math>\omega</math> to <math>\omega</math> there is a [[Tree (set theory)|tree]] <math>T\in M</math> such that for every <math>n</math> the <math>n^{th}</math> level of <math>T</math> has cardinality at most <math>g(n)</math> and <math>f</math> is a branch of <math>T</math>.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Shelah | first = Saharon | authorlink = Saharon Shelah
 | doi = 10.1007/s004930100027
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Combinatorica]]
 | mr = 1832454
 | pages = 309–319
 | title = Consistently there is no non trivial ccc forcing notion with the Sacks or Laver property
 | volume = 21
 | year = 2001| arxiv = math/0003139}}.</ref>

The Sacks property is used to control the value of certain [[cardinal invariant]]s in [[forcing (set theory)|forcing]] arguments. It is named for [[Gerald Sacks|Gerald Enoch Sacks]].

A [[Forcing (mathematics)|forcing notion]] is said to have the Sacks property if and only if the forcing extension has the Sacks property over the ground model.  Examples include [[List of forcing notions#Sacks forcing|Sacks forcing]] and [[List of forcing notions#Silver forcing|Silver forcing]].

[[Saharon Shelah|Shelah]] proved that when proper forcings with the Sacks property are [[iterated forcing|iterated]] using countable supports, the resulting forcing notion will have the Sacks property as well.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Shelah | first = Saharon | authorlink = Saharon Shelah
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-662-12831-2
 | edition = 2nd
 | isbn = 3-540-51700-6
 | mr = 1623206
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag, Berlin
 | series = Perspectives in Mathematical Logic
 | title = Proper and improper forcing
 | year = 1998}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Schlindwein | first = Chaz
 | doi = 10.1007/s00153-013-0361-8
 | issue = 1-2
 | journal = Archive for Mathematical Logic
 | mr = 3151404
 | pages = 171–202
 | title = Understanding preservation theorems: chapter VI of ''Proper and improper forcing'', I
 | volume = 53
 | year = 2014| arxiv = 1305.5906
 }}</ref>

The Sacks property is equivalent to the conjunction of the [[Laver property]] and the <math>{}^\omega\omega</math>-bounding property.
